title: [YouPass Collect] - Higher education qualifications by gender across five countries
prompt: The chart below shows the percentage of males and females with higher education qualifications in five countries in 2001. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the proportions of men and women who held higher education qualifications in five countries in 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, males were more likely to have higher education qualifications than females in the majority of the given countries, with the exceptions being the United States and Germany. Additionally, Switzerland recorded the highest percentage of qualified males, while Germany had the largest proportion of educated females.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the countries where men outnumbered women, Switzerland had the most significant gender gap, with 45% of males holding higher education qualifications compared to just 35% of females. In Japan, the figures were lower for both genders, at 30% and 25% respectively. Meanwhile, Britain reported that 35% of men were highly educated, which was 5% higher than the corresponding figure for women.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining nations, Germany showed the opposite pattern, with 45% of females possessing higher education qualifications, 10% higher than their male counterparts. Similarly, in the United States, women also surpassed men, recording figures of 40% and 35% respectively.
